messages:
maria-cs: Heads-up: client "Crescent" hit mixed 401s and 429s during SDK boot in staging after they changed their edge/WAF. Ticket C-421.
liam-eng: Do we have an example request and whether this is a single host or many?
maria-cs: Single host. Sent sanitized request:
```
POST /v1/generate
Authorization: Bearer <jwt>
Content-Type: application/json
{\"model\":\"redwood-1\",\"input\":\"hello\"}
```
They observe ~1/10 requests 401 and short 429 bursts (~30s windows).
zara-ps: Two likely causes: header rewrite/truncation in proxy/WAF, or very short TTL causing refresh stampede/jwt clock skew. TTL?
maria-cs: Tokens TTL is 15s, many serverless prewarmed lambdas refreshing around same time.
sam-sre: Short TTL + concurrency = concurrent refreshes -> bursts and temporary throttles. Also proxies sometimes drop the Authorization header causing intermittent 401. Ask them to add X-Debug-Id and capture headers.
liam-eng: Recommend this probe:
```bash
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "X-Debug-Id:probe123" https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -d '{"model":"redwood-1","input":"probe"}'
```
We need to confirm header arrival downstream.
maria-cs: Sent probe. Also: deploy-bot: deploy by liam-eng at 2026-03-21T09:12:00Z :rocket:
liam-eng: If nginx is used, ensure `proxy_set_header Authorization $http_authorization;` is present. Missing it can drop auth when proxy chains exist.
zara-ps: Short-term mitigation: increase token TTL to ~60s and add jitter to refresh to avoid synchronized bursts.
maria-cs: Customer logs (tokens redacted):
[2026-03-21T09:20:13Z] 200 OK X-Debug-Id=probe123 req=abc123
[2026-03-21T09:20:13Z] 401 Unauthorized X-Debug-Id=probe124 req=abc124 auth=missing
[2026-03-21T09:20:14Z] 429 Too Many Requests X-Debug-Id=probe125 req=abc125 rate=client_concurrency
[2026-03-21T09:20:15Z] 200 OK X-Debug-Id=probe126 req=abc126
They see Authorization flagged as missing on some requests.
sam-sre: Likely WAF or gateway stripping header or header-size limit. Any CDN/WAF in front?
maria-cs: Yes, they have a managed WAF and API gateway and they updated WAF rules right before the incident.
liam-eng: Ask them to bypass the WAF or tweak rules to forward Authorization unchanged. If 401s stop it's the WAF.
maria-cs: They disabled suspect WAF groups and retried: result 10/10 200s and far fewer 429s after adjusting client refresh.
liam-eng: Agreed next steps: 1) fix or disable WAF rule that mangles headers; 2) raise token TTL to 60s + add jitter to refresh; 3) monitor for 429 windows and we can grant temporary higher rate limits for onboarding if needed.
zara-ps: I'll draft a short onboarding checklist for gateways (nginx, envoy), token TTL guidance, and client refresh jitter examples and share as a gist.
maria-cs: I'll update the ticket with mitigations and request their WAF post-mortem. Thanks all :thumbsup:
liam-eng: Optional: we can provision a temporary elevated ingress window (24h) to smooth their ramp.
maria-cs: Offering that now and closing loop with the customer.
